div.head: Chapter 6
div.p: And that our Indian nations fall within this fourth category, anyone can prove with little effort, even the most simple-minded among us. That they hold and possess their kingdoms and lands by natural law and the law of nations, recognizing no superior, in law or in fact, that is, in act, outside of themselves, as we found them in possession of those kingdoms and with so many principalities and dominions over such infinite numbers of people: by whom they were not only served and obeyed but indeed more than worshipped, their kings and princes freely using and exercising over them all jurisdiction and power, high and low, pure and mixed authority, with no one powerful enough to stay their hand; and their kingdoms and regions so far away and separated from ours by so great a distance, and thus utterly remote from having offended us or the Church or the Catholic faith or any member thereof or any person of the Christian people, or from having had any dealings or vassalage with us. Who, with right judgment, could deny it? Our Indian nations of the west and south are therefore properly and truly of this fourth kind or category of unbelievers.

This is confirmed by a new decree established by Pope Paul III, who in his leaden bull, which begins Sublimis Deus sic dilexit humanum genus, decreeing and declaring: that our Indians and all other nations that shall hereafter come to the knowledge of Christians, although they exist outside the faith of Christ, are not and must not be deprived of their liberty or of dominion over their things; rather they may lawfully use and enjoy their liberty and dominion, and must not be reduced to servitude. And whatever is done to the contrary shall be null and void, of no force or moment; and that the said Indians and the other nations are to be invited to the said faith of Christ through preaching and the example of a good life, by apostolic authority, as we decree and declare by these presents. These are the words of the said decree, in which he makes sufficiently clear that these nations and others like them of this fourth kind — that is to say — contain in themselves no cause of the kinds that are present in the other categories of unbelievers for subjecting them or making them our subjects, nor do we have anything to do with them for good or ill, but only to love them and to labor to help and save them. And consequently, that no king, no emperor, nor the Roman Church may make war upon them or in any way molest them in order to subject them against their will. Whereby this decree manifestly confirms the truthful and Catholic doctrine of Cajetan that was cited above. This second principle is therefore true — that is to say — that there are four kinds or categories of unbelievers, knowledge of which is most necessary for anyone who is to treat of this matter, so as not to err in an intolerable manner. We have treated this at very great length in our work De unico vocationis modo omnium gentium ad veram religionem, lib. 1, cap. 3, s. 85.
